storylines.title: They trailed in every game of the series. They won it anyway.
storylines.observation: The Milwaukee Brewers swept the two-time defending champion Dodgers in the NLCS for their first pennant since 1982, then beat Tampa Bay in five games for the first World Series title in franchise history - a 57-year wait that outlasted a blown 3-0 lead.
storylines.question: What does it mean to win every game of a series without ever actually being ahead until the moment that mattered?
storylines.hidden_question: Does a result like this reveal something real about a team's character, or is it just the kind of statistical oddity that looks meaningful only in hindsight?
storylines.pattern: a decisive, clean-looking outcome built out of narrow, late comebacks rather than sustained dominance
storylines.why_now: Dormant: the arc this card tracks - the comeback pattern through the title and the parade - is complete. The offseason has begun (free agency, trade rumors), but that's a different story than the one this card is telling; holding until a genuinely new angle on the championship itself surfaces.
storylines.season_or_time_context: World Series Game 1 played Oct 23, 2026; Game 2 Oct 24

history.note: Milwaukee held its championship parade Friday, Oct 30: down Wisconsin Avenue at 10 a.m., ending at Henry Maier Festival Park for a free rally. The same city gave the 1982 team a parade after a Game 7 loss - this time there was a title to go with it.

Game 5: Brewers 4, Rays 1. Milwaukee closed out the series 4-1 at Tropicana Field for its first World Series title ever. William Contreras was named Series MVP; Trevor Megill recorded a 6-out save to finish it.

Game 4: Rays 4, Brewers 3 (12 innings). Cooper Pratt's homer put Milwaukee ahead in the top of the 12th; Tampa Bay answered with two in the bottom, Ben Williamson's hit walking it off. Series now 3-1; Milwaukee can still clinch in Game 5.

Game 3: Brewers 10, Rays 1. An eight-run fifth inning - a World Series record, built on seven straight hits - ended any suspense; Milwaukee takes a 3-0 series lead and can clinch the title with a win in Game 4.

Game 2: Brewers 5, Rays 4. Tampa Bay scored four in the top of the first; Milwaukee tied it on Sal Frelick's sixth-inning homer, took the lead in the seventh on a Cooper Pratt RBI, and closed it out - a 2-0 series lead built from another come-from-behind win.

storylines.title: Two countries that made peace in 2018 are undoing it in real time
storylines.observation: Ethiopia and Eritrea severed diplomatic ties on October 1 after the Tigray People's Liberation Front launched a major offensive against federal forces, reviving a conflict both sides had declared over in 2022 and raising fears of a second border war between the two countries.
storylines.question: How much of a peace holds once the leaders who made it decide it no longer serves them?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the 2018-2022 Ethiopia-Eritrea rapprochement better understood as a genuine resolution, or as a pause that lasted exactly as long as both governments found it convenient?
storylines.pattern: a negotiated peace between old enemies unraveling once the domestic politics that made it convenient change
storylines.why_now: Dormant: multiple search passes across several cycles, including this one, have turned up nothing dated past the Oct 16 interim-government announcement - only recycled 2020-2022 Tigray-war coverage and an unrelated Feb 2026 atrocity-accusation story. Holding until a genuinely new, dated development (ceasefire talks, a Western Tigray move) surfaces.
storylines.season_or_time_context: Diplomatic ties severed Oct 1, 2026; fighting resumed late September; interim Tigray government installed Oct 16 with a 6-month election mandate

history.note: No dated development has surfaced since Oct 16 despite repeated search passes; results keep surfacing recycled 2020-2022 Tigray-war material. Going dormant rather than being bumped on a stale source.

The TPLF lost Mekelle and its other strongholds; on Oct 16 Addis Ababa named an interim Tigray administration (a new mayor, chief administrator and security/economic recovery heads) with a 6-month mandate to organize elections. The Western Tigray dispute and the Eritrea rupture remain unresolved.

Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties Oct 1 after Eritrean soldiers were reported entering the Tigray towns of Adigrat and Idaga Hamus; the UN chief called for an immediate end to fighting across Tigray, Afar and Amhara on Oct 9-10, with no ceasefire talks announced since.

storylines.title: A high-school protest over classroom conditions became a nationwide movement about everything else
storylines.observation: What began in mid-September as a lyceens' protest over classroom conditions and the Parcoursup college-admissions platform has grown into weekly nationwide marches over the cost of living, drawing hundreds of thousands and clashes with police in multiple cities.
storylines.question: At what point does a protest about one specific grievance become a vessel for every other grievance a country is carrying?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the scale of a protest movement a measure of the original grievance, or of how much unrelated frustration it happened to be standing near?
storylines.pattern: a narrow, specific grievance absorbing a much larger, diffuse one until the original complaint becomes almost incidental
storylines.why_now: Dormant: no dated development has surfaced since the Nov 7 bilan despite repeated search passes; the next known action point is a coordinated end-of-November protest with partners in six other European countries, not yet dated. Today's Assembly debate is on the 2027 social-security budget bill, a separate story. Holding until a dated development lands.
storylines.season_or_time_context: Movement began mid-September 2026; weekly Saturday marches since, including Oct 17, Oct 24 and Oct 31; general strike held Nov 5

history.note: No dated development since the Nov 7 bilan despite repeated searches; organizers are reportedly coordinating a cross-European action for end of November, not yet dated. Going dormant rather than restating the Nov 7 tally.

The Interior Ministry's official Nov 7 bilan: 146,000 marched nationwide (46,000 in Paris) across 141 actions - down sharply from the 575,000 counted on Nov 5 - with incidents in several big cities, contained by police.

Organizers called a continued 'Acte IV' push for Nov 6-7 - a strike Nov 6 followed by nationwide marches Saturday, Nov 7 - extending the movement a second week past the Nov 5 general strike. Turnout figures for the weekend haven't been reported yet.

Nov 5 general strike: roughly 270,000 marched in 180 demonstrations outside Paris per an early-afternoon Interior Ministry count, with black-bloc clashes in Lyon and incidents in Nantes. Only 81 of 3,700 lycees were confirmed blocked (unions claimed 1,000+); rail disruption was patchy, not a full shutdown.

Ahead of Thursday's five-union general strike, SNCF rail unions confirmed they're joining (a day before the new TGV M's inaugural run) and private-school staff are walking out for the first time - the fight is shifting from weekend marches to a broader work stoppage.

storylines.title: A president trailing in the polls just won anyway - and the loser won't accept it
storylines.observation: Lula da Silva won a fourth term as Brazil's president on October 25, narrowly defeating Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the former president, in the tightest runoff in the country's recent history, after trailing him in most pre-election polls.
storylines.question: What does it mean when the polls and the outcome disagree - does it say something about the polls, or about what happens once people actually vote?
storylines.hidden_question: Is a come-from-behind election win evidence that late deciders broke one way, or a sign that pre-election polling has become less reliable at measuring this kind of race?
storylines.pattern: a result that defies its own pre-vote polling, raising the question of what the polling missed rather than just who won
storylines.why_now: Dormant: the legal fight itself is ongoing (Flavio's abuse-of-power/cassacao filings, Lula's counter-filing against Flavio, both pending before the TSE), but three search passes since Monday turned up nothing dated past Oct 26 - no ruling, no new filing with a confirmed date. Holding until the TSE actually rules on something or a dated development lands.
storylines.season_or_time_context: Runoff held Oct 25, 2026; new term begins Jan 5, 2027

history.note: The TSE confirmed Lula's win. Flavio Bolsonaro announced election night he'd seek to annul the result, then dropped that bid by Monday - his campaign is pivoting to a narrower abuse-of-power claim instead, which allies reportedly see as a longer shot.

Lula won the Oct 25 runoff, 51.79% to 48.21%, despite trailing Flavio Bolsonaro in most pre-election polls and losing the first round to him outright. Bolsonaro says he will challenge the result in court rather than concede.

storylines.title: A new Fed chair's first contested vote
storylines.observation: The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.75%-4% on October 28, Kevin Warsh's first contested decision as chair, with two policymakers dissenting in favor of a hike against a backdrop of inflation still running above target.
storylines.question: What does it mean for a new institution's leadership when its very first contested decision reveals the committee split rather than unified?
storylines.hidden_question: Is a split vote evidence of a healthily independent committee working through genuine uncertainty, or an early sign that this Fed chair hasn't yet built the consensus his predecessor had?
storylines.pattern: a new leader's early decisions get read for what they reveal about authority and consensus, not just the substance of the choice itself
storylines.why_now: Dormant: the next real decision point is the Dec 9 FOMC meeting, and nothing dated has surfaced since the Oct 28 decision despite a search for Warsh's post-meeting remarks - everything found was recycled August Jackson Hole coverage. Holding until a genuinely new, dated development (a speech, a leak, Dec 9 itself) lands.
storylines.season_or_time_context: FOMC meeting concluded Oct 28, 2026; next decision Dec 9, 2026

history.note: The Fed held rates at 3.75%-4% on Oct 28. Governors Cook and Hammack dissented in favor of a hike - up from a unanimous September vote - while new chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal his own view and pointed to December as the next decision point.

storylines.title: Halloween spending keeps hitting records, even as everything about it gets more expensive
storylines.observation: Americans are expected to spend a record $13.5 billion on Halloween this year - costumes, decorations and candy all individually topping $4 billion - even as candy prices have risen three times faster than inflation since 2021 and most shoppers blame tariffs.
storylines.question: Why does a holiday with no functional purpose, that costs more every year, keep getting more popular rather than less?
storylines.hidden_question: Is rising Halloween spending evidence that ritual spending is one of the last discretionary categories people protect even under inflation pressure, or just evidence that retailers have gotten better at making the holiday feel mandatory?
storylines.pattern: a discretionary ritual expense that keeps setting records even as its underlying costs rise faster than overall inflation - spending as a measure of what people refuse to cut
storylines.why_now: Dormant: Halloween has passed and the season's story is complete - a record year, now closed. Holding until next year's NRF survey or a genuinely new angle (post-season retail data, candy-industry followup) surfaces.
storylines.season_or_time_context: Halloween is Oct 31, 2026; NRF survey fielded Sept 1-9, 2026

history.note: NRF's annual survey projects a record $13.5 billion in US Halloween spending this year, with 74% of Americans planning to celebrate - even as candy prices have outpaced inflation threefold since 2021 and most shoppers expect tariffs to push costs higher still.

storylines.title: A 32-meter Catrina and a parade for the dead, scheduled to the minute
storylines.observation: Mexico City's Dia de Muertos season runs Oct 29-Nov 2, anchored by a 32-meter Catrina in the Zocalo and an Oct 31 parade of thousands along Paseo de la Reforma, with downtown building facades lit for the occasion - nearly all of it free.
storylines.question: What does it mean for a ritual of remembrance to be planned with the precision of a civic event - down to the exact height of the centerpiece and the exact route of the march?
storylines.hidden_question: Does scheduling grief this precisely make the ritual more meaningful by giving it shared structure, or does it turn mourning into spectacle once a city plans it like a parade route?
storylines.pattern: a ritual built around loss and remembrance staged with the same civic choreography as a parade or festival - logistics applied to grief
storylines.why_now: Dormant: the official season ended Nov 2 and the observance itself (Nov 1-2) has passed - a complete, closed arc for this year. Holding until next year's season or a genuinely new angle surfaces.
storylines.season_or_time_context: Dia de Muertos observed Nov 1-2; CDMX's official season runs Oct 29-Nov 2, 2026

history.note: Mexico City's Dia de Muertos season (Oct 29-Nov 2) centers on a 32-meter Catrina in the Zocalo and an Oct 31 parade of thousands down Paseo de la Reforma, part of roughly 5,000 events the city is running this season, almost all free to attend.

storylines.title: The country that gave up hosting a climate summit, then volunteered to run it anyway
storylines.observation: COP31 opens Nov 9 in Antalya, Turkey, but Australia - which withdrew its hosting bid in a deal with Turkey - will lead the actual negotiations as 'President of Negotiations,' while the UN's climate chief has already lowered expectations for the summit.
storylines.question: What does it mean to run the talks at a summit you turned down the chance to host?
storylines.hidden_question: Is splitting the hosting country from the negotiating leadership a sign of healthy burden-sharing in climate diplomacy, or evidence that nobody wanted full ownership of a summit expected to produce little?
storylines.pattern: an institution's ceremonial host and its substantive leader are different parties, which raises the question of who actually owns the outcome
storylines.why_now: On Nov 9 the EU and 77 OACPS countries - 104 nations, about 2 billion people, over half the UN's membership - issued a joint declaration naming six shared priorities (adaptation, climate finance, clean electrification, data/science capacity, food-system resilience and ocean governance) ahead of the summit, a bloc-building move distinct from Turkey's own draft Antalya Declaration.
storylines.season_or_time_context: Pacific Pre-COP held Oct 5-8, 2026; COP31 runs Nov 9-20, 2026 in Antalya

history.note: On Nov 9 the EU and 77 OACPS countries - 104 nations, about 2 billion people - issued a joint declaration naming six shared climate priorities ahead of the summit, a separate bloc-building move from Turkey's own draft Antalya Declaration.

Leaders were told to 'get serious' about the climate crisis as the summit opened. Turkey's Kurum says an 'Antalya Declaration' is being drafted but won't gather dust on shelves; Australia's Bowen wants a narrower outcome; the EU says it's arriving empty-handed.

The Antalya Leaders' Summit opens today, Nov 11: Erdogan leads the opening session (12:15-13:30 local) with remarks from UN chief Guterres and Australia's PM Albanese, followed by a gala dinner hosted by Erdogan and the first lady.

COP31 opened today, Nov 9, in Antalya. The UNFCCC's own event page confirms the Leaders' Summit for Nov 11-12, opened by President Erdogan - settling earlier conflicting reports over whether that segment would be in Antalya or Istanbul.

Ahead of the Nov 9 opening, Turkish police detained two trade unionists in Antalya on Nov 3 under NATO-summit-style security measures; organizers now expect close to 100,000 foreign visitors from 196 countries, straining hotel capacity and projecting $1.5-2 billion in economic activity for the city.

storylines.title: A loud election year, a quiet result: every incumbent on the ballot won
storylines.observation: In the first major vote since last year's wave election, New York's Kathy Hochul, Connecticut's Ned Lamont and New Jersey's Cory Booker all won reelection comfortably on Nov 3 - a status-quo night with none of 2025's drama.
storylines.question: What does it mean when an election cycle produces no upsets at all - is a quiet result evidence of stability, or just evidence that nobody was paying attention?
storylines.hidden_question: Is a status-quo election a sign of a healthy, settled electorate, or a sign that the real contest already happened in 2025 and this vote was never competitive to begin with?
storylines.pattern: an election with high pre-vote attention but a fully predictable outcome - the drama front-loaded into the buildup rather than the result
storylines.why_now: Dormant: election night results are the whole story this card tells, and the arc is complete - Hochul, Lamont and Booker's wins are settled with no recount or contested count underway. A search for certification or recount follow-up turned up nothing dated past Nov 4. Holding until a genuinely new angle surfaces.
storylines.season_or_time_context: Election held Nov 3, 2026; contrasts with Nov 2025's Virginia, New Jersey and NYC results

history.note: No recount or certification dispute emerged; a search for follow-up turned up nothing dated past Nov 4. The election-night result is the complete story here, so the card goes dormant rather than being bumped with nothing new.

New York's Kathy Hochul (~60-40 over Blakeman), Connecticut's Ned Lamont and New Jersey's Cory Booker all won reelection comfortably on Nov 3 - a quiet, status-quo night, unlike 2025's competitive Virginia/New Jersey governor races and NYC's Mamdani upset.

storylines.title: A new telescope's first month of data turned up a world ten years of looking had missed
storylines.observation: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory's new Simonyi Survey Telescope found 2026 ED138, a trans-Neptunian object 46 AU from the sun and possibly 600-1,500 km wide, hiding in archival images dating back to 2016 - a potential sixth dwarf planet nobody had flagged until now.
storylines.question: What does it mean that a new instrument's first months of data turned up something a decade of sky surveys had already photographed and missed?
storylines.hidden_question: Is this a story about how much of the solar system remains unmapped, or about how much depends on which telescope happens to be pointed at the right patch of sky at the right time?
storylines.pattern: a new tool reveals, in its very first pass, something that was already there in old data all along - visible only in hindsight
storylines.why_now: Dormant: 2026 ED138 remains an unconfirmed candidate awaiting infrared follow-up (likely JWST) to settle its size and shape; repeated search passes find the same unchanged status, no new dated development. Holding until a confirmation, a scheduled observation, or an IAU decision lands.
storylines.location: Cerro Pachon, Chile (Vera C. Rubin Observatory)
storylines.season_or_time_context: Observations taken Mar 4-Jul 11, 2026, plus archival images back to 2016; announced Oct 27, 2026

history.note: Still an unconfirmed candidate awaiting infrared follow-up; repeated searches find the same status as the initial announcement, nothing newly dated. Going dormant rather than restating the same facts.

Rubin Observatory announced Oct 27 that 2026 ED138, a trans-Neptunian object ~46 AU out and 600-1,500 km across, was found in its first months of survey data and traced back through archival images to 2016 - a dwarf-planet candidate pending confirmation.

storylines.title: The same festival, the same five days, a different set of rules in every city that marks it
storylines.observation: Diwali's fixed five-day arc - Dhanteras on Nov 6 through Lakshmi Puja on Nov 8 to Bhai Dooj on Nov 10 - is set by the lunar calendar, but how it's marked varies by city, from unrestricted fireworks to tight bans.
storylines.question: What does it mean for a ritual fixed by astronomy to look completely different depending on which country's laws and customs it lands in?
storylines.hidden_question: Is Diwali's adaptability across diaspora communities a sign of a tradition's resilience, or evidence that a ritual's practice simply bends to whatever restrictions its host city imposes?
storylines.pattern: a globally observed ritual whose core timing is fixed by astronomy but whose practice is reshaped city by city by local law and custom
storylines.why_now: Dormant: the main night (Lakshmi Puja, Nov 8) has passed and no dateable 2026 coverage of the celebrations or their aftermath has surfaced despite repeated searches - the usual post-Diwali air-quality story hasn't been reported yet either. storylines.season_or_time_context: Dhanteras Nov 6, Lakshmi Puja (main night) Nov 8, Bhai Dooj Nov 10, 2026

Diwali's main night falls Nov 8 within its five-day arc (Dhanteras Nov 6 to Bhai Dooj Nov 10); diaspora cities mark it on different terms - NYC's Times Square celebration already ran Oct 24, and personal fireworks stay tightly restricted even as temples hold pujas this weekend.

storylines.title: The same mountain's snowcap went from latest in 130 years to early - with the ruler changed in between
storylines.observation: Mount Fuji's first snowcap of the season arrived Oct 30, 2026 - seven days earlier than usual under Japan's newly adjusted observation method - a sharp reversal from 2024's latest snowcap in 130 years of record-keeping and 2025's 21-days-late arrival.
storylines.question: What does it mean when a years-long warming trend reverses in the very same year the method used to measure it changes?
storylines.hidden_question: Is Mount Fuji's early snowcap this year real evidence the warming trend eased, or mostly an artifact of switching to a new way of declaring 'first snow'?
storylines.pattern: a reversed trend that arrives at the exact moment the measurement method itself changed, leaving real signal and methodological artifact tangled together
storylines.why_now: Dormant: the story is the single fact of the reversal itself (an early snowcap under a revised method, after two years of record-late ones) - there's no further development to track, and a search for follow-up found nothing new. Holding until next year's comparison or a genuinely new angle surfaces.
storylines.season_or_time_context: First snowcap observed Oct 30, 2026; compares to Nov 7, 2024 (latest on record since 1894) and Oct 23, 2025

history.note: No further development to report - the story is the single fact of the early snowcap itself. Going dormant rather than restating the same facts.

Mt. Fuji's first snowcap arrived Oct 30 under a newly adjusted observation system, about seven days earlier than the old method would show - a reversal after 2024's snowcap was the latest in 130 years of records and 2025's came 21 days late.

storylines.title: A padlock sealed in 1583 finally opened - the four-letter code inside still means nothing to anyone
storylines.observation: A CT scan let Cardiff University researchers crack the code on a 1583 shipwreck's brass combination lock - the four letters 'ANCE' opened it, but nobody knows what the word meant to its owner.
storylines.question: What does it mean to finally solve a 443-year-old puzzle and have the answer turn out to be a different, unsolvable one?
storylines.hidden_question: Is cracking the mechanism without understanding the meaning behind it really a resolution, or just a more precise description of what we don't know?
storylines.pattern: a technical problem gets solved completely while the human question behind it - why this code, what it meant - stays exactly as open as before
storylines.why_now: More detail on the find: the Ann Francis was sailing home to Norfolk from Spain when it wrecked on Margam Beach near Port Talbot in a December 1583 storm; the lock and coin hoard are now on public display in the 'Tides of Treasure' exhibit at the National Waterfront Museum, Swansea. What the cracked code meant to its owner is still unknown.
storylines.location: Cardiff, Wales (shipwreck off the Welsh coast)
storylines.season_or_time_context: Ship wrecked Dec 1583; hoard recovered 1996-2017; code cracked and announced Nov 4, 2026

history.note: Additional detail: the Ann Francis was sailing home to Norfolk from Spain when it wrecked on Margam Beach near Port Talbot; the lock and hoard are now on public display in the 'Tides of Treasure' exhibit at Swansea's National Waterfront Museum.

Cardiff University and National Museum Wales announced Nov 4 that a CT scan let them crack a 1583 shipwreck lock's combination - 'ANCE' - confirmed by opening the physical lock undamaged. What the code meant to its owner, or what it protected, remains unknown.

storylines.title: Yields fell for two weeks straight after the Fed's first contested vote - the opposite of what the dissenters wanted
storylines.observation: The 10-year Treasury yield slid from 5.07% on Oct 23 to roughly 4.86% by Nov 6 - a two-week decline that began right after the Fed's Oct 28 hold, even though two governors dissented in favor of a hike and inflation is still running above target.
storylines.question: What does it mean when the bond market moves in the opposite direction from what the loudest voices on the policy committee wanted?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the market's declining yield a vote of confidence that inflation will cool on its own, or a sign that growth worries are starting to outweigh the inflation concern the dissenters raised?
storylines.pattern: a market move runs counter to what a committee's most vocal members pushed for, which raises the question of who actually reads the underlying data correctly
storylines.why_now: Dormant: the card tells a complete, closed story - the two-week yield decline through Nov 6 - and a search for a more current reading found nothing dated past that. Holding until a fresh yield move or Fed-adjacent development justifies an update.
storylines.season_or_time_context: Yield measured Oct 23-Nov 6, 2026; spans the Fed's Oct 28 rate decision

history.note: No fresher yield data found; the story is the complete two-week decline through Nov 6. Going dormant rather than restating the same figures.

The 10-year Treasury yield slid from 5.07% (Oct 23) to about 4.86-4.90% (Nov 6), a two-week decline spanning the Fed's Oct 28 hold, where two governors dissented in favor of a hike - the market moving the opposite way from the dissenters.

storylines.title: An American football game was played inside the most famous soccer stadium in the world
storylines.observation: The Bengals beat the Falcons 34-17 at Real Madrid's Bernabeu Stadium on Nov 8 - the NFL's second regular-season game in Madrid and Cincinnati's first ever in Spain - with roughly 80,000 fans filling a stadium built for an entirely different sport.
storylines.question: What does it mean for a century-old American sport to go looking for new fans inside the most famous stadium of a completely different one?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the NFL's international expansion into stadiums like the Bernabeu building real new fandom, or just renting attention from a crowd that came for the building, not the game?
storylines.pattern: an institution borrows another institution's cathedral to stage itself, testing whether the audience that shows up for the building also stays for the sport
storylines.why_now: The Bengals beat the Falcons 34-17 on Nov 8 at the Bernabeu, Real Madrid's home ground - only the second NFL regular-season game played in Madrid (after the 2025 Dolphins-Commanders game) and the first-ever NFL game in Spain for Cincinnati. Joe Burrow threw three touchdowns and ran for a fourth in front of a crowd organizers expected to reach about 80,000, the latest step in the league's push to grow its European audience.
storylines.season_or_time_context: NFL Week 9 game played Nov 8, 2026; Madrid's second NFL regular-season game after the 2025 Dolphins-Commanders game
